events_chronological: Insurance investigator Martin Kray interviews a claimant named Elias Prine and rules his memory loss psychosomatic, denying the claim.
Elias's diabetic wife tests him by asking for injection after injection, and dies of the overdose he cannot remember giving her.
Intruders attack Martin and his wife in their bathroom; Martin kills one and is struck in the head, losing the ability to form new memories.
Martin builds a system of instant photographs, annotated notes and tattoos to hunt the second attacker, a man he knows only by the initials R.M.
About a year before the main action, a plainclothes officer called Roy helps Martin find and kill the real attacker, a killing Martin forgets within minutes.
In a motel room he cannot remember checking into, Martin narrates the Prine case down the phone to an anonymous caller.
Martin burns his wife's hairbrush and books in a field, trying to grieve a loss he can never retain.
The caller feeds Martin a name and a location, identifying the drug dealer Gil Marsh as the man he is looking for.
Martin beats and strangles Gil in a derelict basement and photographs the body.
As he dies Gil whispers "Elias", which Martin cannot explain, and Martin changes into the dead man's suit and takes his sports car.
Roy arrives and tells Martin that Gil was innocent, that Martin already avenged his wife a year ago, and that Martin is himself the man in the Prine story.
Rather than believe him, Martin burns the photographs of Gil, writes "he is lying to you" on Roy's picture and copies down Roy's licence plate as his next target.
Martin drives to a tattoo parlour and has the plate inked on his thigh as the sixth fact.
At her bar, Gil's girlfriend Corinne recognises the dead man's clothes and car and serves Martin a beer the staff have spat in.
Corinne hides every pen in her house, goads Martin into hitting her, then returns bruised and blames a man called Vance so that Martin will go after him.
Martin ambushes Vance in a motel bathroom, beats him and drives him out of town at gunpoint.
Corinne runs the licence plate through a friend at the vehicle registry and hands Martin a record naming Roy Mercer.
Martin lures Roy to the derelict building, shoots him in the head and photographs the corpse.
nonlinear_category_reason: Two strands on a strict alternating beat - the colour thread running backwards, the black-and-white thread forwards - with each colour scene explained by the one that follows it.
syuzhet_notes: Two threads alternate. The colour scenes - told-order bullets 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 and 14-18 - run in reverse chronological order, each beginning where the previous one started. The black-and-white motel scenes - told-order bullets 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12 and 13 - run forward. The two threads meet at told-order bullet 14, when the film turns to colour mid-scene and then plays forward to the end. Told-order bullets 4, 6 and 10 are flashbacks to before the head injury.
fabula_notes: The officer's account of bullets 5 and 11 is asserted rather than dramatised, and it is left undecided whether the claimant material is a case the investigator worked or a displaced account of his own wife's death, so the placement of the first two bullets is the most defensible reading rather than a settled fact.

events.content: Working a claim from behind a desk, Martin puts a soft-spoken man through test after test and writes the memory loss down as something the mind is doing to itself. The insurer pays nothing.

Elias: nobody will pay for his care
reader: intro:Martin
intro:Elias
a man with no new memories was refused help

questions.q8: why does Martin keep returning to this one old case?

events.content: Unable to believe the condition is real, his wife puts her watch forward and asks for her injection, then asks again, and again. He gives her each one as though it were the first.

reader: a man with no memory can be made to kill by repetition

events.content: Two men come through the bathroom door at night. Martin shoots one of them across his wife's body and is put into the mirror head first by the other, and from that moment nothing new will stay.

Martin: a second man got out of the house
reader: intro:Martin's wife
Martin can no longer form new memories

questions.q10: was the second man ever found?

events.content: Martin turns himself into a filing cabinet: instant photographs captioned in block capitals, notes clipped to notes, and the facts he trusts most cut into his own skin where he cannot lose them.

Martin: he must trust his own handwriting over his own head
reader: the hunt is run entirely on notes Martin himself writes

events.content: A plainclothes officer walks Martin through the evidence, finds the second man in a building out past the edge of town, and stands by while Martin shoots him. Within minutes Martin is asking who they are looking for.

Roy: Martin can be given the same ending over and over
reader: intro:Roy
the revenge already happened and did not stay

events.content: In a room he cannot remember taking, Martin sits on the end of the bed with the receiver against his ear and tells the old claim story to somebody who already seems to know how it ends.

reader: Martin is talking to somebody he cannot identify

questions.q7: who is on the other end of the telephone?

events.content: Out in a field Martin feeds a hairbrush and a paperback into a small fire, waiting to feel something end. He cannot hold the loss long enough to finish grieving it.

Martin: grief will not complete itself in him
reader: Martin cannot mourn what he cannot retain

events.content: The voice on the telephone gives Martin a name, a trade and an address, and tells him where the man will be. Martin writes it all down as fact.

Martin: the man he wants is a dealer called Gil
reader: the target was supplied, not found

events.content: In a basement with water on the floor Martin beats a man half his weight, gets a belt round his throat, and holds it until it is over. Then he takes the picture.

reader: intro:Gil
Martin has killed on a name he was handed

questions.q9: was the dealer the man who attacked Martin's wife?

events.content: The dying man says a single word that means nothing to Martin, who writes it off and cannot ask again. Martin changes into the dead man's suit, takes his keys, and drives his car away.

Martin: the dead man knew a name Martin cannot place
reader: Martin is now wearing and driving a dead man's life

events.content: The officer sits Martin down and lays it out: the dealer was nobody, the revenge was taken a year ago, and the case Martin recites to strangers down the telephone is not a case at all but his own house.

Martin: he has already had his revenge
he has been killing to have something to do
reader: Roy has been steering Martin from the beginning

events.content: Rather than hold a truth that would leave him nothing, Martin burns the photographs, writes three words across the officer's picture, and copies the registration off the car outside as the next thing he will be certain of.

Martin: he can choose what he will have known
reader: Martin has knowingly falsified his own record

events.content: Martin walks into a parlour with a note in his fist and has the registration inked down his thigh under the five facts already there. He does not remember writing the note.

Martin: the plate belongs to the man who killed his wife
reader: a lie has been promoted to a permanent fact

questions.q6: why is this registration the sixth thing Martin trusts?

events.content: Behind her own bar a woman watches a stranger come in wearing a suit she knows and park a car she knows outside. She smiles, takes his order, and has the staff do something to the beer before it reaches him.

Corinne: the man in her bar is why nobody has come home
reader: intro:Corinne
somebody has worked out what Martin did

questions.q4: why do the staff of this bar treat the stranger the way they do?

events.content: She clears every pen out of the house first. Then she says the things that will make him swing, waits outside until the bruises come up, and comes back in blaming a man he has never met.

Corinne: he can be aimed like a dog
Martin: a man called Vance beat her
reader: Martin's condition makes him a weapon anyone can borrow

questions.q5: why does this woman want Martin in her house at all?

events.content: Martin waits in the dark of another motel bathroom, takes the man down as he comes through, and drives him to the edge of town with a gun in his ribs and a warning he will not himself remember giving.

reader: intro:Vance
Martin has hurt a man on a stranger's say-so

questions.q3: why is Martin so certain this man is guilty of anything?

events.content: She has a friend at the registry run the plate off the note he leaves lying about, and puts the printout into his hand across the table with a name on it in full.

Martin: the plate belongs to a man named Roy Mercer
reader: the false fact has now been given a face and an address

questions.q2: where did Martin get a registration to run in the first place?

events.content: Martin brings the officer out to the same derelict building on a pretext, walks him into the room, puts one through his head and photographs what is left, satisfied that the note was right.

reader: Martin has executed a man on a fact he wrote himself

questions.q1: why is Martin so sure this is the man he has been hunting?

edges.on: the story of a man who kills his wife with injections he cannot remember giving
